title: The Hotfix
brief: A hotfix HF-208 is proposed for the Meridian Digital payroll export, which a customer needs for its month-end run in 2 days. The fix changes the rounding logic. You have 12 visit points to assess whether the change has been reviewed for risks, controls, and records before it is deployed.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Account manager: has the customer been told
Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: HF-208 states the reason, the customer impact, and the affected component. Approval section is pending.
evidence.whyItMatters: The record describes the change and its purpose.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The record is in order for its stage.

evidence.text: Emergency change procedure EC-2 allows a shortened review but requires peer review, targeted testing, an approver, and a rollback plan.
evidence.whyItMatters: A defined route for urgent change exists.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The procedure is sound. The question is whether HF-208 follows it.

evidence.text: Peer review of HF-208 was approved by the author's own second account (reviewer ID dev-17b for author dev-17).
evidence.whyItMatters: Review must be independent of the author to be effective.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check reviewer and author identities, not only the approval tick.

evidence.text: Test results for HF-208 show 4 unit tests passed; no test uses the customer's month-end data volume of about 40,000 records.
evidence.whyItMatters: Verification should show the change meets the requirement in the conditions that matter.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask whether the tests reflect the real use.

evidence.text: Rounding logic is shared by invoices and tax reports; the regression scope for HF-208 lists payroll export only (scope note 2).
evidence.whyItMatters: Risks to other outputs affected by a change must be considered.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask what else uses the changed code.

evidence.text: Customer contract clause 14 requires 5 working days' notice of changes to calculation logic, or written agreement to a shorter period. No agreement is on file.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer requirements on change notification must be met.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read the contract for change notice terms.

evidence.text: Account manager: "I mentioned a fix was coming in a call on day 1, but nothing in writing yet."
evidence.whyItMatters: Informal contact has started; a written record of agreement would complete it.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask what has been communicated and how.

evidence.text: Deployment plan includes a tested rollback to the previous build within 15 minutes.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A tested rollback is good practice.

evidence.text: Post-deployment monitoring plan MP-208 lists error rate only; no check of rounding totals against a reference file is planned for the first run.
evidence.whyItMatters: Monitoring the result that the change affects would confirm it works. This is an improvement opportunity.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask how the team will know the change worked.

evidence.text: Release manager: the head of operations or deputy approves emergency changes; both are available today.
The release calendar shows a freeze starting in 3 days.
evidence.whyItMatters: A planned freeze is a scheduling fact, not a nonconformity.

evidence.text: Hotfix names follow the convention HF-number, but one older hotfix used lower case.
evidence.whyItMatters: A naming slip on an old record does not affect this change.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Naming style is not a requirement breach here.

options: Only after independent peer review, testing at month-end volume across payroll, invoices, and tax reports, approval under EC-2, and written customer agreement to the shorter notice
No, wait for the next quarterly release
Yes, but do not tell the customer to avoid alarm
decisions.rationale: The emergency procedure allows speed but not skipped controls. The listed steps can be done within 2 days.

containment: Do not deploy HF-208 until EC-2 conditions are met
correction: Obtain independent review, extend tests to all users of the rounding logic, and record customer agreement
cause: The tooling allows self-review through a second account, and the emergency procedure has no impact checklist for shared code
corrective: Block approvals by linked accounts; add a shared-component impact check to EC-2
effectiveness: Audit the next ten emergency changes for independent review and impact checks

debriefText.found: You checked independence, test depth, shared risk, and the customer's terms.
debriefText.missed: In an urgent change, look for the controls that the hurry removed.
debriefText.falseFinding: A calendar freeze and an old naming slip are not issues with this change.
